[Textbook inconsistency in the printed hint: the key's formula is correct and the answer below matches it character for character, but the hint printed alongside it says the effective acceleration due to gravity "will get reduced" by the radial acceleration. The key's own formula has \(g_{\text{eff}} = \sqrt{g^{2} + (v^{2}/R)^{2}}\), which is GREATER than \(g\) — the two accelerations are perpendicular, so they add in quadrature and the effective value increases. The key refutes its own hint; the formula is the half to trust.]
